places.name: GARDEN WALK observation deck, T1 5F
places.note: Reopened 9 April 2026 after a full year shut (closed 7 Apr 2025), rebuilt as part of SHIKISAI GARDEN on 5F. Free. The airport publishes only the opening: 06:30. Seasonal pattern is 1 Apr–30 Sep 06:30–21:00, 1 Oct–31 Mar from 07:00, so on 15 Sep it is open well before the group lands. The old mesh fence is gone — wire now, and a raised timber Mountain Deck to shoot over it.
places.confidenceNote: The 06:30 opening and the Mountain Deck and footbaths are in Narita's own press release; the 21:00 close and the Apr–Sep / Oct–Mar split are not on any current official page and come from pre-renovation published hours.

places.name: T1 landside food: 4F restaurants and the 5F SKY FOOD COURT
places.nameJp: 4階レストラン街・5階スカイフードコート
places.note: CORRECTION to the seed line that nothing trades before 07:30. McDonald's, T1 Central Building 4F landside, runs 06:30–21:30 (L.O.) and is open before the coach arrives. The 5F SKY FOOD COURT sits inside SHIKISAI GARDEN — ramen, udon, pasta counters — and the 5F area itself opens 05:00. Note the T1 Ippudo is 3F AIRSIDE, 07:30–20:30 (L.O.), not on these floors.
places.confidenceNote: McDonald's and Ippudo hours are from the airport's own shop pages; the individual SKY FOOD COURT tenants' hours are not published anywhere — the operator states only that the 5F area opens 05:00, and the tenant list is from a visitor review.

places.name: LAWSON Narita Airport Terminal 1 B1F
places.nameJp: ローソン 成田空港第1ターミナルB1F店
places.note: 00:00–24:00, before security. This matters more than it looks: Narita states that T1's upper floors run 05:00–24:00 and only 1F and B1F are open 24 hours, so this is the one shop that is certainly trading whatever time the coach gets in. It is also a designated zipper-transparent-bag store — the place to buy the 1-litre clear liquids bag. Tel +81 476-30-3020.
places.confidenceNote: Hours, floor and the transparent-bag designation are from the airport's own shop page; the coordinate is the government geocoder's T1 address point (千葉県成田市古込1番地), building level, not the B1F unit.

places.name: Capsule Marche, T1 Central Building 5F
places.note: 05:00–23:00, before security, 5F — the earliest-trading shop above ground level in T1 and next door to the deck. Gachapon capsule machines, which is the tidiest way to get rid of leftover ¥100 and ¥500 coins before a flight home: notes can be changed, coins cannot. Anyone waiting for the 07:55 counter can be sent here rather than standing in the lobby.
places.confidenceNote: Location and the 05:00–23:00 hours are from the airport's own shop listing; the coin denominations the machines take are not published by the shop, and the coordinate is the 5F deck point rather than the unit.

places.name: SHIKISAI GARDEN relaxation rooms (Cha-no-ma, I-no-ma, Sho-no-ma)
places.nameJp: 茶の間・居の間・書の間
places.note: 130 free seats in four spaces round the 4F–5F atrium — tatami, sofas, planting, seasonal scent — and on paper the best sit-down in the building for a group with an hour to kill. THE CATCH: Narita's own release gives their opening as about 13:30. At 08:30 they are shut. Do not plan the wait around them; the deck, the food court and the 4F shops are what is actually open.
places.confidenceNote: The 13:30 opening and the 130-seat count are from Narita's own press release and a trade report of the opening; the coordinate is the 5F deck point, not a surveyed position for the rooms.

places.name: GARDEN WALK footbaths, north end of the 5F deck
places.note: Three real hot-water footbaths, each about 5 m by 0.8 m, at the NORTH end of the deck beyond the Mountain Deck, free, one of them scented with seasonal bath salts. Before 8h25 of seat time and eleven hours door to door this is the best twenty minutes in T1. Bring a small towel from the room — no towel service is published — and do it after the bags are gone, not before.
places.confidenceNote: Narita's release confirms the footbaths exist on the renewed deck and a press visit reports them as free; no official page publishes footbath hours or a towel policy, so the deck's own 06:30 opening is assumed.

places.name: Narita Nakamise, T1 South Wing 3F (AFTER security)
places.note: CORRECTION: Narita Nakamise is the T1 SOUTH WING 3F mall AFTER security, not a 4F landside street. The airport's own shopping-area page puts it airside on 3F, and Fa-So-La's shop list prints the address as 第1ターミナル 南ウイング3F narita nakamise. Roughly 07:30–22:00. It is exactly where SQ637's passengers end up, so the omiyage run belongs here, after immigration.
places.confidenceNote: The 15-minute leg assumes security and passport control are moving; it is 4F counter to 3F South Wing airside via both, not a measured walk. Coordinate is the geocoded T1 address point.

places.name: Fa-So-La GIFT SHOP Terminal 1 South Wing, 4F
places.nameJp: Fa-So-La GIFT SHOP 成田空港第1ターミナル南ウイング店
places.note: 07:00–20:00, before security, on the SAME FLOOR AND WING as the Singapore Airlines counter — famous sweets from around Japan. This is the earliest-opening souvenir shop in T1 and the only real one trading if the coach gets in before 07:30, which is why it is the answer to a 07:00–07:30 dead half hour. Two minutes from the check-in island. Tel +81 476-33-1917.
places.confidenceNote: Hours, floor, wing and the before-security position are from the airport's own shop page and Fa-So-La's own site; the coordinate is the geocoded T1 address point, building level.

places.name: TOKYO SHOKUHIN KAN OMOTASE-DOKORO, T1 Central 4F
places.nameJp: 東京食賓館 おもたせ処
places.note: 07:30–21:00, before security, T1 Central Building 4F, and a designated TAX FREE SHOP: long-established Japanese confectioners next to the current national best-sellers, under one roof. Tel +81 476-32-8685. This is the real landside sweets shop, and it opens 07:30 — which is exactly why a coach that leaves the hotel at 06:00 buys nothing for the first ninety minutes.
places.confidenceNote: Coordinate is the government geocoder's T1 address point (千葉県成田市古込1番地); the airport publishes no unit-level position. Hours, floor and tax-free status are from its own shop page.

places.name: Fa-So-La TAX FREE AKIHABARA Terminal 1, SW 3F airside
places.nameJp: Fa-So-La TAX FREE AKIHABARA 成田空港第1ターミナル店
places.note: 07:30–22:00, after security, South Wing 3F inside Narita Nakamise, with an annex on the same floor and the same hours. The airside confectionery specialist: its own brand pages name Tokyo Banana, ROYCE' and ISHIYA Shiroi Koibito, and the maneki-neko chocolate is a Narita exclusive. Tel +81 476-33-1917. This, not a landside street, is the last shop of the trip.
places.confidenceNote: Hours and the airside 3F South Wing position are from the airport's shop page and Fa-So-La's own store list; the coordinate is the geocoded T1 address point and the leg assumes security and immigration are clear.

places.name: Fa-So-La DUTY FREE Terminal 1 South Wing, 3F airside
places.nameJp: Fa-So-La DUTY FREE 成田空港第1ターミナル南ウイング店
places.note: 07:30–21:00, after security. Perfume, cosmetics, Japanese whisky, cigarettes. Two Malaysian limits first: Royal Malaysian Customs exempts 1 LITRE of liquor per adult, and cigarettes and tobacco are EXCLUDED from the traveller exemption altogether — no duty-free cigarette allowance into Malaysia at all. Bottles are cabin-legal only because they are bought airside.
places.confidenceNote: Coordinate is the geocoded T1 address point. Hours and the airside 3F position are from the airport's own shop page; the allowances are from the Royal Malaysian Customs traveller guide.

places.name: DRUG BOX Terminal 1 South Wing, 4F
places.nameJp: ドラッグボックス 成田空港第1ターミナル南ウイング店
places.note: 07:00–21:00, before security, 4F South Wing, tax-free — the last pharmacy of the trip and it opens at 07:00, before the counter does. Motion-sickness tablets, painkillers, eye drops and compression socks for 8h25 of seat time. Also a designated zipper-transparent-bag store, so the 1-litre clear liquids bag is here too. Tel +81 476-33-2139.
places.confidenceNote: Coordinate is the geocoded T1 address point, building level; hours, floor, wing, tax-free and transparent-bag status are from the airport's own shop page.

mustSee.title: GARDEN WALK observation deck, Narita T1 5F
mustSee.nameJp: 成田空港第1ターミナル 展望デッキ「GARDEN WALK」
mustSee.summary: Free, open from 06:30, and the only place in the building where 35 people can spread out for a last group shot without blocking anyone. Rebuilt and reopened 9 April 2026 after a year closed: the old mesh fence replaced by wire, a raised timber Mountain Deck to see over it, and three hot-water footbaths at the far end.
mustSee.whereToFind: T1 5F. Through the SHIKISAI GARDEN atrium and out the deck door. Climb the MOUNTAIN DECK — the raised timber mound about 2.5 m above deck level — and stand on the top with your back to the terminal, looking EAST across the apron and down Runway A; from the flat deck the fence is 3 m high and in every frame, from the mound it is not. The wire is spaced about 7 cm, so a phone lens goes through it. At 08:30 the sun is in the east-south-east and fairly high, so face the group WEST with their backs to the fence: faces lit, aircraft behind them, no flare. The footbaths are at the far NORTH end, past the mound.
mustSee.confidenceNote: The 06:30 opening, the Mountain Deck and the footbaths are from Narita's own release; the 2.5 m mound height, the 3 m fence and the 7 cm wire spacing are from a trade report of the opening, not an official page.

Fleet of Narita Airport Transport, for Narita Airport terminal connection bus (toll free). Model: Mitsubishi Fuso Aero Star KC-MP747M License plate: CBC200 KA-152 Place: Narita Int

mustSee.title: Narita Nakamise, T1 South Wing 3F — after security
mustSee.summary: The airport's biggest concentration of Japanese sweets and the trip's actual last shared activity — 35 people buying omiyage together. It is NOT the 4F landside street the seed described: the airport's own shopping-area page and Fa-So-La's store list both place Narita Nakamise on 3F of the South Wing, after security, roughly 07:30–22:00.
mustSee.whereToFind: Airside, not landside. From the Singapore Airlines counter on 4F South Wing, security and passport control drop you onto 3F; turn into the South Wing and Narita Nakamise is the single main axis running away from the central building. Stand at the Fa-So-La TAX FREE AKIHABARA frontage, roughly the middle of the street, with the shopfronts running left to right behind the group — that fills the frame with signage and keeps the walking lane open down one side. Face back toward the central building so the street recedes behind you.
mustSee.confidenceNote: Coordinate is the government geocoder's T1 address point (千葉県成田市古込1番地); Narita publishes no coordinate for an airside mall, so this is building level and the seed's 140.3929 has been dropped as it sits about 600 m east of the terminal.

mustSee.title: The 35-in-one-frame shot, 4F South Wing check-in hall
mustSee.nameJp: 第1ターミナル 南ウイング4階 出発ロビー
mustSee.summary: The day's outfit note asks for the one photograph where all 35 people are in one place, indoors and unhurried — and this is the only moment it exists. Bags are gone, the counter queue has cleared, nobody is carrying anything, and the flight is still two hours away. It never happens on any other day of the trip.
mustSee.whereToFind: 4F South Wing departure lobby. Put the group with their backs to the Singapore Airlines check-in island so the carrier signage sits above their heads, and shoot from the concourse side with the wing's window wall BEHIND THE CAMERA, not behind the group — the 4F glazing is bright at 08:40 and shooting into it silhouettes everyone. Leave the trolley lane clear on the camera side. Do it after the last bag is tagged, about 08:40, not while the queue is still forming.
mustSee.confidenceNote: The floor and wing are Narita's own published allocation for Singapore Airlines, but neither the airport nor the airline publishes the counter island's letter or number, so the exact position within the 4F South Wing lobby is not verified.

shopping.name: The omiyage run at Narita Nakamise
shopping.placeLabel: Narita Nakamise, T1 South Wing 3F — AFTER security, roughly 07:30–22:00
shopping.note: CORRECTION: this is the airside 3F South Wing mall, not a 4F landside street, so the run happens after immigration — plan 09:50–10:25, not before check-in. ¥5,000 is a realistic per-head budget. One ceiling to say out loud: Royal Malaysian Customs exempts only RM1,000 of other goods per adult arriving by air, about ¥30,000, so the heavy shoppers should keep receipts.
shopping.confidenceNote: The ¥5,000 figure is a planning budget, not a quoted price. Coordinate is the geocoded T1 address point.

shopping.name: ROYCE' Nama Chocolate [Au Lait], 20 pieces
shopping.nameJp: ロイズ 生チョコレート[オーレ]
shopping.placeLabel: Fa-So-La shops, T1 South Wing 3F airside — ANA FESTA's Narita stock is the T2 lobby shop only, which the group never reaches
shopping.note: ¥1,215 for 20 pieces. ROYCE' prints 要冷蔵 — refrigerate at 10°C or below — with about a month's shelf life. Be honest with the group: Narita 10:55 to Penang 20:35 is eleven hours plus transfer and an ice pack will not hold 10°C that far. It arrives soft, not spoiled. Ice and gel packs ARE allowed in hand baggage. Want pristine? Buy ROYCE' bar or potato-chip chocolate instead.
shopping.confidenceNote: Price, piece count, 要冷蔵 and shelf life are ROYCE's own product page, and ROYCE's shop list places its Narita stockists in the airside gate and duty-free areas — but no official page names the specific T1 unit holding refrigerated nama chocolate, and ANA FESTA lists Narita stock only at the T2 lobby shop.

shopping.name: ISHIYA Shiroi Koibito tins, 18 and 24 pieces
shopping.placeLabel: Fa-So-La TAX FREE AKIHABARA, T1 South Wing 3F airside; also the 4F landside confectionery shops
shopping.note: ¥1,320 tax-free for the 18-piece tin and ¥1,760 for 24, on Fa-So-La's own price list. Room temperature, a rigid tin, langue-de-chat with a chocolate layer — the one item here that arrives in Penang exactly as it left, with nothing to melt into anything else. It is heavy for its size, so count it against the 7 kg or pad it flat in the checked bag.
shopping.confidenceNote: Prices are Fa-So-La's own published tax-free prices for its Narita shops; the coordinate is the geocoded T1 address point.

shopping.name: Tokyo Fugetsudo Gaufre tin, 12 wafers
shopping.nameJp: 東京凮月堂 ゴーフル
shopping.placeLabel: T1 Central Building 4F landside confectionery — TOKYO SHOKUHIN KAN OMOTASE-DOKORO, 07:30–21:00, tax free
shopping.note: ¥1,620 for the 12-wafer tin, ¥594 for 5, ¥2,592 for the 16-piece twin tin — and 180 days from manufacture, by far the longest shelf life of anything on this list. That is what makes it the office box rather than a personal gift. The wafers are thin and snap: carry the tin FLAT, never on edge, and never loose in a checked bag.
shopping.confidenceNote: Prices and the 180-day shelf life are the maker's own retail list; no Narita shop page names Fugetsudo specifically, so the 4F landside confectionery shop is the likely rather than the confirmed stockist.

shopping.name: Tokyo Banana Mii-tsuketa, 8 pieces
shopping.nameJp: 東京ばな奈「見ぃつけたっ」
shopping.placeLabel: Fa-So-La TAX FREE AKIHABARA (T1 South Wing 3F, airside) and the 4F landside sweets shops
shopping.note: ¥691 / ¥1,296 / ¥1,944 for 4, 8 and 12 pieces — identical at the maker, at JAL PLAZA and at ANA FESTA, so it is not marked up at the airport. It is sponge cake with banana custard inside: it crushes, and its best-before runs in days not weeks. So it rides on TOP of the hand baggage and it gets eaten in Penang that week, not saved for a shelf.
shopping.confidenceNote: Prices are the maker's own and match two airport retailers' product pages; the maker publishes no shelf life, so 'days not weeks' is inferred from a fresh-cream sponge product, not from a printed figure.

shopping.name: ISHIYA Maneki-neko Chocolate, 24 pieces — Narita exclusive
shopping.nameJp: 石屋製菓 招き猫チョコレート
shopping.placeLabel: Fa-So-La shops at Narita — the exclusive was launched at TERMINAL 1 only
shopping.note: ¥1,400 tax-free for 24 pieces, 8 each of white, milk and matcha-milk, in a lucky-cat box — a Narita Airport exclusive that Fa-So-La launched at Terminal 1 only. If anyone wants a souvenir that genuinely cannot be bought in Tokyo or Penang, this is it, and today is the only day of the trip it is reachable. Room temperature, boxed, and it travels like the Shiroi Koibito tins.
shopping.confidenceNote: Price and the Terminal-1-only line are Fa-So-La's own, but that page is dated February 2024 and says expansion to Terminals 2 and 3 was planned, so the exclusivity may have widened since.

shopping.name: Japanese whisky, one 700 ml bottle per adult
shopping.nameJp: ジャパニーズウイスキー（免税）
shopping.placeLabel: Fa-So-La DUTY FREE Terminal 1 South Wing, 3F — after security, 07:30–21:00
shopping.note: The limit first: Royal Malaysian Customs exempts 1 LITRE of intoxicating liquor per adult arriving by air, and cigarettes and tobacco are excluded from the traveller exemption entirely — there is no duty-free cigarette allowance into Malaysia. One 700 ml bottle per adult is safe; two is not. Buy it AIRSIDE: a bottle bought landside would breach the 100 ml cabin rule at security.
shopping.confidenceNote: The allowances are quoted from the Royal Malaysian Customs traveller guide. The ¥6,000 estimate is an indicative mid-range figure — the shop publishes no price list.

shopping.name: One-litre clear resealable liquids bag
shopping.placeLabel: LAWSON T1 B1F (24 hours) or DRUG BOX T1 South Wing 4F (07:00–21:00) — both designated zipper-transparent-bag stores
shopping.note: Narita designates certain shops as zipper-transparent-bag stores and both of these are on the list — which matters at 07:15 when nothing else is open. One bag per person, containers 100 ml or under, 1 litre total. Anything over 100 ml bought in Tokyo yesterday has to move into the CHECKED bag before the counter shuts at 10:15, and after that there is no second chance.
shopping.confidenceNote: The transparent-bag designation and both shops' hours are from the airport's own shop pages; the ¥150 estimate is indicative, as neither shop publishes a price.

Narita Airport — Terminal 1 South Wing.closedNote: T1 is NOT a 24-hour building in the way Haneda T3 is. Narita states that most floors — including the 4F check-in lobby and the 5F deck — run 05:00–24:00, and that only 1F and B1F are available 24 hours. OPEN at 08:30 on Tue 15 Sep: GARDEN WALK observation deck 5F from 06:30 (1 Apr–30 Sep 06:30–21:00), McDonald's 4F Central 06:30–21:30 L.O., Fa-So-La GIFT SHOP 4F South Wing 07:00–20:00, DRUG BOX 4F South Wing 07:00–21:00, Capsule Marche 5F 05:00–23:00, LAWSON B1F 24 h, TOKYO SHOKUHIN KAN OMOTASE-DOKORO 4F Central 07:30–21:00, and airside on 3F South Wing: Narita Nakamise, Fa-So-La TAX FREE AKIHABARA 07:30–22:00, Fa-So-La DUTY FREE 07:30–21:00, Ippudo 07:30–20:30 L.O. NOT OPEN at 08:30: the SHIKISAI GARDEN relaxation rooms, which the airport's own release opens at about 13:30, and Kinder Platz at 10:00 — so the free 130-seat lounge cannot be part of the plan.
Narita Airport — Terminal 1 South Wing.lastAdmission: 10:15 — Singapore Airlines' own table for Narita closes check-in and baggage acceptance 40 minutes before the 10:55 departure. That is the day's real deadline, not the boarding time.
Narita Airport — Terminal 1 South Wing.groupRate: None to buy — the terminal, the GARDEN WALK deck and the three footbaths are free, and there is no admission anywhere in the building. The group discount that does exist is tax-free: at 15 Sep 2026 Japan still deducts consumption tax AT THE TILL, minimum ¥5,000 per shop per day, passport or Visit Japan Web code presented at the cashier. There is no departure refund counter to queue for.
Narita Airport — Terminal 1 South Wing.phoneNote: Narita Airport general information, open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year — the only number the airport publishes; there is no separate Terminal 1 or South Wing line. Singapore Airlines in Japan: +81 3-4578-4088, the number printed on Narita's own Singapore Airlines page. A group send-off desk in the 4F South Wing lobby answers 06:30–22:00.
Narita Airport — Terminal 1 South Wing.tickets: SQ637 NRT→SIN 10:55, TERMINAL 1 SOUTH WING, 4F — that is Narita Airport's own published allocation for Singapore Airlines, printed as 'T1 South Wing / 4F' on its airline page. The app prints no terminal anywhere, so this is now confirmed from the airport rather than inferred. Singapore Airlines' own airport table for Narita: counters OPEN 3 hours before departure (07:55) and CLOSE 40 minutes before (10:15). Narita separately advises arriving at least two hours before. Baggage 25 kg checked, 7 kg hand-carry, one piece. Power banks under SQ's rule effective 15 Apr 2026: cabin only, never checked, maximum two, up to 100 Wh without approval, kept in the seat pocket or under the seat and NOT in the overhead bin, and not charged from the in-seat outlet or used to charge anything in flight. Ground handling in the South Wing publishes a group reception desk at K counter no. 16.
Narita Airport — Terminal 1 South Wing.transport: Tour bus from International Resort Hotel Yurakujo, 650-35 Nanae, Tomisato. The app prints '~15 min' with NO clock time; the hotel itself quotes about 20 minutes, so budget 20–25. Working back from 10:55: counter opens 07:55, so stand the group at the 4F South Wing counter by 07:50, which means at the kerb 07:25–07:35 and off the hotel forecourt at 07:00–07:10. That fits the app's 06:30 breakfast (the restaurant's own opening minute, so ask for a pre-set group section). It does NOT fit the briefing PDF's '6.00am Depart from hotel', which lands the group at T1 about 06:20 — ninety minutes before the SQ counter opens, before the observation deck opens at 06:30, and before breakfast could have happened at all. Both are recorded; neither is resolved here. Drop-off is the 4F departure kerb, South Wing.

subRoutes.title: Bags gone first, then the deck: the landside hour

steps.name: GARDEN WALK deck, 5F — the group shot
steps.note: Straight up from the counter the moment the last bag is tagged. Mountain Deck, backs to the fence, faces to the west. Free, open since 06:30.

steps.name: Footbaths at the north end of the deck
steps.note: Optional and worth it before 8h25 of seat time. Shoes off, own towel, three baths so about ten people at a time — not all 35.

steps.name: 5F SKY FOOD COURT or 4F McDonald's
steps.note: Named here only as the fallback for anyone who skipped the 06:30 hotel breakfast — McDonald's on 4F has been open since 06:30. Zero minutes in the plan; peel off individually.

steps.name: TOKYO SHOKUHIN KAN OMOTASE-DOKORO, 4F Central
steps.note: The landside tax-free sweets shop, open since 07:30. Passport to the cashier, ¥5,000 minimum per shop per day. Buy the boxes, not the chilled.

steps.name: Fa-So-La GIFT SHOP, 4F South Wing
steps.note: Two minutes from the security queue, so it is the last landside stop by design. Anything missed here reappears airside at Fa-So-La on 3F.

subRoutes.note: The order is the whole point: only one thing today has a hard closing time, and it is the counter. Check in at 07:55, then this hour is hands-free with the bags already gone. Deadline 09:45 at the South Wing security queue — half an hour before check-in closes at 10:15 and a clear hour before boarding, which is the margin 35 people and one passport queue actually need.
subRoutes.confidenceNote: Every shop's hours are official, but the internal walking minutes are paced off the published floor layout, not measured, and the 09:45 security handover assumes a normal morning queue rather than a published wait time — Narita does not publish live security waits for T1 South Wing.

subRoutes.title: Airside on 3F: the omiyage run you actually get

steps.name: Narita Nakamise, South Wing 3F
steps.note: Regroup and headcount at the head of the street the moment everyone is through passport control. Say the get-back-by out loud here: 10:25.

steps.name: Fa-So-La TAX FREE AKIHABARA + annex
steps.note: The chilled ROYCE', the Shiroi Koibito tins, Tokyo Banana and the Narita-only maneki-neko box. Buy the refrigerated item LAST, on the way out.

steps.name: Fa-So-La DUTY FREE, South Wing 3F
steps.note: Liquor only, and only one litre per adult for Malaysia. No duty-free cigarette allowance into Malaysia at all — skip the tobacco wall.

subRoutes.note: Thirty-five minutes, and it is the only shopping the group is guaranteed to get — everything landside depends on the coach being on time, this does not. It exists because Narita Nakamise turned out to be AFTER security, not before, which moves the whole omiyage plan to the far side of immigration. Get-back-by 10:25 at the gate: boarding a 7-hour widebody starts around 10:15–10:25 and there is no slack behind it.
subRoutes.confidenceNote: Shop hours and the airside 3F South Wing positions are official; the gate is not assignable in advance and the seed's 'gates via Satellite 3' claim could not be verified, so the walk to the gate is not costed here.

Narita Airport — Terminal 1 South Wing.photo: Two frames and two completely different lights. On the 5F GARDEN WALK deck at 08:30 you are outdoors under a high east-south-east sun with a pale concrete deck, new timber and a grey apron behind — bright, flat and unforgiving, so mid-tone solids read and white blows out. In the 4F check-in hall you are indoors against cool-white ceiling light and a bright glazed wall; anything black disappears, anything white glares. If the trip has a shirt or a company colour, today is the day it is worth wearing: it is the one photograph with all 35 people in one place, indoors, unhurried. Plain colours over prints — 35 people in patterns is noise at any distance. Nobody should be holding a coffee cup or a passport wallet in the group frame.
Narita Airport — Terminal 1 South Wing.practical: Tokyo is 32°/25° today and the deck is in full sun by 08:30, then a 7-hour cabin held near 23°C, a 2h15 connection in Singapore's air conditioning, and Penang at 20:35 still warm and humid. That is one light long-sleeve you can take off and put back on four times, not a jacket you have to carry. Slip-on shoes: one security screening, one passport control, and shoes off again at the deck footbath. Compression socks for 8h25 of seat time. Weigh in the room, not at the counter — 25 kg checked, 7 kg hand-carry, ONE piece. The two rules that go opposite ways: every battery, phone, camera and power bank must be in the CABIN and is banned from the hold, with a maximum of two power banks, kept in the seat pocket or under the seat and never charged or used in flight; while anything liquid over 100 ml goes the other way, into the CHECKED bag before the counter closes at 10:15. Under-100 ml bottles need one 1-litre clear resealable bag per person, sold at LAWSON B1F and DRUG BOX 4F. A small towel in the hand baggage for the footbath. Passport out, not packed: tax-free is still deducted at the till today, so every shop needs to see it.
